clue.text: Spiritual energy almost completely enveloping that place

indicators.note: almost means falling just short, so the word for completely loses its final letter
to envelop is to wrap around, so the outer letters close around the phrase for that place

blocks.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
all, as in 'all gone', means completely
there means in or at that place

explanation.surface: A description of someone's spiritual energy almost entirely enveloping a particular place.
explanation.walkthrough: Almost completely reads as one adverb phrase, but almost trims the word for completely, and the trimmed word joins energy to form the wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ethereal is delicate and otherworldly, a close synonym of spiritual in the sense of not of this material world.

clue.text: Sinner — top, rampant player at Wimbledon?

indicators.note: rampant suggests running wild and unchecked, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written; Jannik Sinner is a top Italian tennis player
taken as written

explanation.surface: Jannik Sinner, the world's top player, playing rampantly at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinner looks like the subject of a sports report, but the name is just letters to rearrange together with top.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimbledon is the famous London tennis championship, so a professional competing there is an example of the answer, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Uplifting story about comic’s last, dazzling show

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting something up means reading it from bottom to top, that is backwards
last points to the final letter of the word comic
about means surrounding, so the reversed word goes around the selected letter

blocks.note: a tale is a story
final letter of comic

explanation.surface: An inspiring tale about a comedian's final, dazzling performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat, borrowed from French, means brilliant effect or conspicuous success, the impression a dazzling show makes.

clue.text: Spreadsheet software, fast and very good

blocks.note: Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet program
Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A recommendation for spreadsheet software that is quick and of high quality.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast reads as an adjective meaning quick, but here it is the noun: a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent is a straightforward adjective synonym for outstanding or of very high quality.

clue.text: England footballer’s nasty insoles

indicators.note: nasty implies something has turned bad or messed up, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that an England player's shoe insoles are unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lionesses is the nickname of England's women's national football team, so any of its players is one.

clue.text: Book to travel around a capital city

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the phrase is read backwards

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
taken as written
to go is to travel
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to reserve a trip around a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogota is the capital city of Colombia, so it is a specific example of the definition.

clue.text: Not just one variable type of Highland accommodation

blocks.note: both means two, more than just one
Y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A note that Highland lodgings come in more than one varied type.
explanation.walkthrough: A bothy is a simple hut or shelter in the Scottish Highlands, often left open for hill walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bothy is a basic stone shelter found in remote Scottish hills, one kind of lodging in that region.

clue.text: Foreign money invested in flashy major tournament

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so these letters go inside the other word

blocks.note: glam, short for glamorous, means showy or flashy
the rand is South Africa's currency; rands are foreign money

explanation.surface: Overseas cash is pumped into a showy, prestigious sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: The rand is the currency of South Africa; the plural is needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand slam is one of the four biggest tennis or golf championships, each a major competition in its sport.

clue.text: Minor adjustment that’s initially lacking oomph

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the preceding word is kept

blocks.note: first letter of that's
something weak lacks power or oomph

explanation.surface: A small change that, at first, has no real punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a slight fine-tuning change made to improve something, which is a small alteration.

clue.text: Central parts of opened tables lock together

indicators.note: the central parts of each word are its middle two letters, which are the ones kept

blocks.note: middle two letters of opened
middle two letters of tables
middle two letters of lock

explanation.surface: The middle sections of extending tables click together when opened.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase en bloc means all together as a single unit, rather than separately.

clue.text: Absent superior reportedly given an embargo

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or said, so the word for superior is taken by its sound

blocks.note: someone who is out is not present
a lord is a superior or master; in a non-rhotic accent it is pronounced like this spelling

explanation.surface: An absent boss is said to have imposed a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pronunciation LORD has no sounded R, so it matches LAWED.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, so something outlawed has been prohibited by such an order.

clue.text: Craft project including new trellis for plant

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the following word's letters are rearranged
including means holding within, so the outer word wraps around the rearranged letters

blocks.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home craft work
taken as written

explanation.surface: A home project building a new garden trellis to support a climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant looks horticultural given the trellis, but it is the industrial sense: a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant can mean an industrial works, and a distillery is the works where spirits like whisky are made.

clue.text: Peer appointed to welcome king

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the outer word holds the letter for king

blocks.note: an appointed time is a due or scheduled time
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A newly appointed nobleman gets ready to greet the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is the highest rank of the British nobility, and members of that nobility are called peers.

clue.text: Informal work detail primarily involving extra cash

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: spec is casual shorthand for a specification, the detailed requirements of a job
first letter of involving
first letter of extra

explanation.surface: A casual job description that mainly mentions some extra payment.
explanation.walkthrough: Extra cash reads as one phrase, but extra gives only a letter and cash alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie means money in the form of coins rather than notes, a formal word for hard currency.

clue.text: Don’t be daft, and get down from there!

blocks.note: first meaning: an exclamation of disbelief, telling someone to stop talking nonsense
second meaning: read literally, an order to climb off something

explanation.surface: A parent scolding a child who has climbed onto the furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for 'stop pretending or exaggerating', and literally a command to descend from a perch.

clue.text: Ought the queen to take responsibility?

blocks.note: ought and should both express obligation
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword abbreviation for the queen

explanation.surface: A question asking whether the monarch ought to accept the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden is to bear it, so shouldering a duty means accepting the burden of it.

clue.text: Working with intention to protect those people in rehab, perhaps

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it, so the outer letters go around the words for those people

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
an end is an aim or intention, as in 'to that end'
them refers to those people

explanation.surface: A worker whose aim is to protect patients in a rehabilitation clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in rehab is one example of recovering, and the idiom for recovering from illness or trouble is this phrase.

clue.text: Attendants infuriate hosts out at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and lost, so the preceding word is scrambled
a host holds guests inside, so the word for infuriate surrounds the other letters

blocks.note: to enrage is to infuriate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cabin crew annoy their hosts while far out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants and followers who accompany an important person.

clue.text: Fatalistic person’s disposition turned endlessly severe

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the word for disposition is read backwards
endlessly means without an end, so the final letter of the word for severe is dropped

blocks.note: a mood is a temperament or disposition
stern means strict or severe

explanation.surface: A gloomy person whose mood has turned harsh without end.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s after person stands for 'has', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A doomster is someone who constantly predicts disaster, a pessimist resigned to a fatalistic outlook.

clue.text: Criticism of Thatcher’s position supporting Republican

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting part sits underneath, so the thatcher's position is placed after the Republican

blocks.note: Rep is a short form of Republican in US politics
a thatcher works on a roof, laying straw

explanation.surface: Criticism of former Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher's political stance, backed by a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatcher looks like the Prime Minister, but it is a tradesman who thatches roofs; supporting means below in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke or expression of disapproval, so it is a form of criticism.

clue.text: Shakshuka base made by mother in toto

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the word for mother sits within the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A cooking note: the shakshuka sauce was made entirely by Mum.
explanation.walkthrough: In toto, Latin for completely, looks like part of the phrase but supplies letters for the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakshuka is a North African dish of eggs poached in a spiced tomato sauce, so tomato is its base.

clue.text: Effusive old German guy

blocks.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive or effusive
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An elderly German man who is gushing in manner.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is common British shorthand for over the top, meaning excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a traditional German male first name, so it fits a man from Germany.

clue.text: Three, maybe five characters in pastel colours

indicators.note: five characters in tells you to take a five-letter run sitting inside the following words

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: A count of three or five letters forming pastel shades.
explanation.walkthrough: Three is a UK mobile phone network, not a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A telco is a telecommunications company, and Three is a British mobile phone operator, so it is an example.

clue.text: Sweet substance coming from purple yams, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the preceding letters can be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sugary product that might be made from purple yams, the sweet tubers.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple syrup is a sweet thick liquid made from the boiled sap of maple trees.

clue.text: Leading European state

blocks.note: main means principal or leading
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A top European country.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is one of the fifty United States, in New England in the far northeast.

clue.text: Sing in a high range?

blocks.note: surface reading: sing with a high vocal register, like a soprano
setter's reading: a range is also a chain of mountains, so this is singing in the Alps

explanation.definitionFit: Yodelling is the warbling singing style of Alpine herders, switching between chest voice and falsetto among the mountains.

clue.text: Cook in the end abandoned one knockout lamb dish

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word cook

blocks.note: final letter of cook
something abandoned has been left
I is the Roman numeral for one
KO is the standard abbreviation for knockout in boxing

explanation.surface: A chef finally gives up on one stunning lamb dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Cook looks like the instruction for the dish, but only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kleftiko is a Greek dish of lamb slow-baked in a sealed pot or parcel.

clue.text: Attract ultimate musical talent

blocks.note: the end is the final, ultimate point
having an ear for music means having musical aptitude

explanation.surface: Supreme musical skill draws people in.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone liked or cherished, winning their affection, so it means draw fondness.

clue.text: Kid with extremely eerie, devilish look?

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the outer letters of the next word are kept

blocks.note: a kid is a young goat
outer letters of eerie

explanation.surface: A child with a really spooky, demonic appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: Kid suggests a child, but it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatee is a small pointed chin beard, the kind traditionally drawn on the Devil, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Final piece from Vivaldi taken on by musician is tricker to manage

indicators.note: the final piece of a word is its last letter, which is kept here
taken on by means absorbed into, so the musician word swallows the selected letter

blocks.note: a fiddler is a violin player
last letter of Vivaldi

explanation.surface: The last movement of a Vivaldi piece proves hard for the violinist to play.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'tricker' is a misprint for trickier.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddly means awkward and needing delicate handling, so the comparative means harder to deal with.
